column1: # Patches the tool catalog is allowed to call VERIFIED, and the real save that
# proves each one.
# verify-tools.mjs applies the patch's decrypt chain — exactly the codes the
# page's Decrypt button runs, via toolkit.js splitChain() — to the encrypted
# sample, and requires the result to equal the decrypted one byte for byte.
# A patch that is not listed here, or that fails, is not marked verified.
# Samples come from bucanero/save-decrypters (not vendored; pass its path).
# Paths are relative to that checkout.
# NO PATCH IN apollo-patches. These C tools have nothing to drive, so the page
# cannot list them however good the sample is: MGS3 HD - Snake Eater,
# CoD Black Ops (PS4), Dead Island 2, MC4 Cheat Decrypter, No Man's Sky,
# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection, Terraria, Middle-Earth: Shadow of
# Mordor and Shadow of War, Resident Evil 3 Remake, Resident Evil Resistance,
# Resident Evil 6 (PS4), PS2 APA Header Checksum. Two more look like a patch
# exists but do not: "Digimon World Next Order" resolves only to Digimon
# Story: Cyber Sleuth, and "Tomb Raider VI: Angel of Darkness Remaster" only
# to Tomb Raider: Definitive Edition. Different games.
# NOT YET LISTED, nothing known against them — the samples do not look like
# save pairs, which is why they were not tried: ff13-decrypter (ff13-1/2/3 are
# 128/160/192 bytes) and mgs-hd-decrypter (mgs2, mgs3, 256 bytes each) read as
# key or test vectors rather than saves. Both have patches on main.
# Not listed, deliberately:
#   PS3/BLUS30554, PS4/CUSA09084  L.A. Noire — its required codes take an
#       interactive {TAG} choice, `{ST}0001=Game Savedata;0002=User Profile`,
#       and the two branches are genuinely different saves, so nothing but the
#       user can pick. Note this is a PAGE gap, not a sample gap: the samples
#       for BOTH branches are already in save-decrypters (SAVEDATA.enc/.dec
#       and SAVEDATA.profile.enc/.dec, plus the PS4 pair). The day the tools
#       page can offer a patch's {TAG} options, four rows go straight in.
#   PS4/CUSA07713  Monster Hunter World — decrypts correctly but exhausts the
#       MicroPython heap under wasm on its 8MB save (MemoryError, not
#       corruption). Revisit when the heap story improves.
#   PS3/BLES00485, PS3/BLUS30270  Resident Evil 5 (PS3) and
#   PS3/BLES01465 et al  Resident Evil 6 — both C tools ship a PS4-shaped
#       sample, not a PS3 one: re5-checksum-fixer's savedata.bin is the very
#       file that proves PS4/CUSA04437, and re6's has the byte-identical
#       16-byte header, with 0x00000008 at offset 0x8 where the PS3 patch
#       writes its DWADD. So the PS3 patches cannot be proved by it (measured:
#       "changed a valid save"). RE5 PS4 is already listed; RE6 has no PS4
#       patch in the database at all, so its sample proves nothing today.
#       Needs a PS3 DATA0.DAT sample for each.
#   PS3/BLES01880, PS3/BLUS31211, PS3/BLJM61093  Final Fantasy X / X-2 HD —
#       two REQUIRED codes that are alternatives, not a sequence: "Update
#       Checksums Final Fantasy X" (writes 0x64F4, range 0x40..0x64F7) and
#       "...Final Fantasy X-2" (writes 0x16268, range 0x40..0x1626B). Both
#       also write the shared header hash at 0x1A, so running the pair over an
#       X save leaves the X-2 hash there and the save is rejected — measured,
#       the harness reports "changed a valid save". Nothing here can pick for
#       the user: it is the SAVE that decides which applies. Needs the two to
#       become a {TAG} choice, or separate :file targets, upstream.
#   PS3/BLES01945, PS3/BLUS31270  Call of Duty: Ghosts — patch and C tool
#       cover DIFFERENT files. The savepatch fixes Adler32 over SAVEGAME.SVG
#       and is the only code in it; save-decrypters' cod-checksum-fixer (and
#       its sample) is MPDATA. So the sample cannot prove the patch. Needs a
#       SAVEGAME.SVG sample, not a manifest row.
# MULTI-TARGET is supported (toolkit.js chainTargets/routeChain): a patch whose
# required chain spans several ':file' targets gets one file slot per target,
# and each code is applied to the file its own target names. Dead Space 3,
# Prototype, Kingdom Hearts HD 2.5 ReMIX and LUNAR Remastered are listed below
# and pass. Two rows in that class still cannot be listed, and neither wants
# the feature:
#   PS3/BLES01040 et al  Dead Space 2 — deadspace-checksum-fixer ships ONE
#       HED-DATA/USR-DATA pair and it is a Dead Space 3 save: BLES01733 passes
#       against it and BLES01040 does not. Needs its own pair.
#   PS4/CUSA12555  Dying Light 2, and PSV/PCSE00608, PSV/PCSF00728,
#       PSV/PCSG00594  Resident Evil: Revelations 2 (Vita) — CONTAINER
#       patches, deliberately left out. Their middle codes target
#       `~extracted\00000000.dat`, which apollo_apply_code reads and writes as
#       a BSD variable rather than a file, so what a run produces is a
#       recompressed container. That is not byte-comparable to the original —
#       zlib is not obliged to reproduce the input stream and measurably does
#       not (Revelations 2 Vita: 39,163 bytes in, 38,601 out; the reference C
#       tool unpacks both to the same payload). Proving one would mean reading
#       the payload back out of the engine's variable list, which is an
#       apollo-lib API this project is not adding. Both tools DO have sample
#       pairs (vita-re-rev2-unpacker, dl2-unpacker) if that ever changes.
# SAMPLE AND PATCH DISAGREE — the C tool and the savepatch are not looking at
# the same bytes. Not a harness limit and not a page limit; somebody has to
# work out which of the two is right. All measured as "changed a valid save":
#   PS3/NPUB31564, PS3/BLJM61144  Samurai Warriors 4 / Sengoku Musou 4 —
#       sw4-checksum-fixer's DATA.BIN fails every SW4 patch, both endian modes.
#   PS3/NPEB01297, PS4/CUSA00057  Strider — same, with
#       strider-checksum-fixer's SaveData against `:SAVEGAME` and `:*`.
#   PS4/CUSA01587  Shantae: Risky's Revenge — the patch updates a JHash over
#       `:savedata.sav`; the unpacker's sample is a 152-byte `savegame`, and
#       the code does not react to it at all.
#   PS3/BLES01894  Need For Speed: Rivals — the patch is fine; its SAMPLE is
#       not. USR-DATA is 716800 bytes but only the first 358404 were ever
#       encrypted, so no correct implementation can reproduce the .enc from
#       the .dec. Re-list it when the pair is regenerated from a real save.
# Waiting on a branch merge — the fixes exist, just not where the page reads
# from. The site fetches patches from apollo-patches@main at run time, so what
# matters here is main, not what is queued for the next console release:
#   PS3/NPUB30611, PS3/NPEB00686  MGS: Peace Walker — main still calls
#       `DECRYPT mgs_pw` with no save-type argument, so it decrypts nothing.
#       Fixed on branch mgs-pw-psp.
#   PS3/BLES00450, PS3/BLUS30248  NFS: Undercover — main still decrypts
#       `pointer+0x5B`, one block short of what apollo-lib has needed since
#       63f334a. Fixed on branch nfs-undercover-range.
# Re-add these four rows when those branches reach main; they pass against the
# branch content today (checked against each branch in a worktree).
# PS4/CUSA18008  Resident Evil Village needs NO row of its own. The patch had
# 11 cheat codes and no checksum code, so there was no step to run; it now
# carries the same "[Update Murmur3-32 checksum (Required)]" as RE7's
# CUSA03842 — which is exactly what save-decrypters' re7-checksum-fixer does
# for Village (murmur3_32 over len-4, seed 0xFFFFFFFF, into the trailing u32).
# Byte-identical code means the expansion pass below proves it from RE7 for
# free, the moment the patch reaches apollo-patches main. Listed here anyway
# because it was also checked directly against village-data001Slot.bin: valid
# save unchanged, and it reacts to a changed byte.
# The mgs-pw-psp branch also adds PSP Peace Walker patches — ULUS10509 and
# ULES01372 (mgs_pw(1)), NPJH50045 (mgs_pw(2)). They are correct, and this
# harness still cannot list them, because "equal to the reference plaintext"
# is the wrong test for them: libapollo deliberately leaves the 0x44-byte
# header word-swapped on PSP, so a savepatch reads the header fields the same
# way on PS3 and PSP. Measured against the shipped samples, the payload from
# 0x44 on is byte-identical and the header is exactly the word-swapped
# reference header — which is the documented convention, not a defect (see
# apollo-lib tests/test_samples.c, known_answer_mgspw_psp).
# Listing them needs a per-row comparison mode ("payload from offset N"), not
# a new sample. Worth doing when PSP coverage matters; not worth blocking the
# first release on.

# ---- checksum fixers ----
# These rows carry "-" as the expected file: the sample IS a valid save, and
# the patch has to leave it byte-for-byte alone. That is a real check — the
# sample holds the checksum the game itself wrote, so a wrong range, algorithm
# or write offset lands somewhere else — and the harness additionally pokes a
# byte and requires the checksum to move, so a code that quietly does nothing
# cannot pass by standing still.
# Each sample is attributed to the patch's own game: either the filename names
# the title ID, or the tool in save-decrypters covers exactly one game, or the
# filename echoes the game name. Samples that cannot be attributed are not
# used — several tools there cover a family of games that share one algorithm
# (the RE Engine ones, the Trails ones), and "a Resident Evil save proves the
# Monster Hunter Rise patch" is not a claim worth making. Patches left out
# this way are mostly picked up anyway by the identical-chain expansion.
